page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-128 is a compute-focused instance within the N2D family, provisioned with 128 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM. The instance runs on dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture across 64 physical cores with two threads per core. Each core provides 32 KB of L1 data cache and 0.5 MB of L2 cache, supported by 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The configuration does not include GPUs or bundled local storage, requiring attached persistent storage volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant parallel compute capabilities. In stress-ng, multi-core CPU throughput reaches 172613.68, placing it in the top 10%, while single-core performance ranks in the top 25% at 2694.18. PassMark scores reflect similar strengths, achieving 89602.52 in overall CPU, 136640.77 in cryptographic tests, and 14281.93 in physics simulations. Geekbench evaluations show top-tier ray tracing results at 100141.0 and solid clang software compilation marks at 52465.0. Memory throughput sustains 263.09 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 131.24 GB/sec for writes.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge from the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. While static web serving achieves 48.86 GB/sec and Redis SET operations handle 120.13 million operations per second, memory-constrained data science and large model execution show limitations. Small and medium language models process prompts efficiently, but large 70B model token generation drops to a weak 2.67 tokens per second due to memory and accelerator constraints. Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by high CPU density per unit of memory rather than massive RAM scaling.

Workloads best aligned with the n2d-highcpu-128 include large-scale CI/CD build farms, batch video encoding, parallel scientific simulations, cryptography-heavy operations, and high-concurrency microservices that prioritize raw processor parallelism over in-memory database capacity.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-128 is a compute-centric server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 128 vCPUs derived from 64 physical cores alongside 128 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server includes no GPUs and offers no local disk storage, necessitating remote persistent block storage. Benchmark assessments establish strong multi-threaded capabilities, registering top-tier results in multi-core stress testing, cryptographic operations, physics calculations, and ray tracing. However, with only 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU and lack of AVX-512 extensions, memory-intensive processes and large-model LLM generation scale less effectively. The instance delivers robust efficiency for CPU-dense tasks, making it suited for distributed compilation, parallel batch processing, encryption workloads, and web serving clusters.
